history_folded_hint: Cleared from the history: undoing this change takes them back too
dash_expand_hint: The charts across the whole window: no header or navigation
dash_ahead: ahead of the plan ({hours} due by now)
dash_behind: behind the plan ({hours} due by now)
dash_burnup_hint: The plan climbs to the total; the green line is what is done so far.

docs_unavailable: The guide could not be loaded here: open it on its site
reschedule_hint: Move the open sessions by days or hours, or re-balance one calendar: more sessions a day to finish sooner, fewer to ease the weeks, or evenly up to its deadline. Done sessions stay; every change can be undone from the history.
reschedule_deadline_hint: Finish before this day; kept as the calendar's deadline
reschedule_pace_hint: Sessions per study day: weekdays without holidays. When the weeks are full, sessions wait and the course ends later.
reschedule_finish_hint: Spreads the open sessions evenly up to this day: the later the day, the later each session.
timeline_keys: Arrow keys move it a day, Page Up and Page Down a week, Home and End to the ends. Enter applies, Escape cancels.
help_timeline:
Each course in its colour, from its first to its last session: a dot is a session, a filled one is done, one with a red ring was missed. ◆ is the course's deadline, hatching is the spare time before it, red after it is late.
Drag a course to move its open sessions by weeks, its end to re-balance it towards a new finish, ◆ to move the deadline; or pick a course and change it on the panel. Changes gather in a draft drawn over the plan as it is: a dashed line shows where the course was. Review the draft, then apply or discard it.
reschedule_over_budget: May go over {hours} h a week
reschedule_reason_nothing_to_move: The calendar has no open sessions from this day on.
reschedule_reason_full_weeks: The weeks of {from} – {to} are full: widen the study hours or allow going over the budget to finish sooner.
reschedule_reason_late: Fits {placed} of {total} sessions before {deadline}: a later deadline, wider study hours, going over the budget or starting the course sooner with Move would help.
reschedule_reason_no_lab_block: “{title}” needs two free hours in a row, and the study hours have none.
reschedule_reason_limit: Some sessions find no room within a year: widen the study hours or allow going over the budget.
reschedule_reason_not_proven: The search stopped at its time limit, so a better placement may exist.
spent_hint: Your pace and the finish forecast are worked out from this time.
log_done_hint: Choose how long each one took. A session left without a time is marked done without one, and the pace does not count it.
log_fill_hint: Choose how long each one took. A session left without a choice stays as it is.
unlogged_bar: Done sessions without a time: {count}. The pace leaves them out.
resize_done_hint: Its length in the calendar is the plan. Did it take a different time, or should the plan change?
focus_like_course: Sessions like this took {ratio} · n {count}: about {time}
focus_like_kind: Sessions of this kind in all courses took {ratio} · n {count}: about {time}
dash_strip_hint: One mark per session with a logged time, on a log scale: ×2 and ×0.5 lie equally far from the plan. Right of the line it took longer.
dash_strip_none: No session has a logged time yet. Each one you log adds a mark here.
dash_strip_n_wait: n {count} · a typical session from {min} logged
help_strip: Every session with a logged time is a mark: a circle for a study session, a triangle for a lab, a square for a review. Its place is the time it took divided by its plan, on a scale where ×2 and ×0.5 lie equally far from the line of the plan. From 6 logged sessions a course also shows its typical session, the diamond, with the band it lies in with 95% certainty; with fewer, a summary would be a guess. Hover a mark to see its session, or Tab to a row and walk it with the arrow keys, Home and End; the table under the chart lists them all.
dash_trend_hint: The line is a course's typical session after each logged one, the band where it lies with 95% certainty. A band that narrows is the estimate settling; a line that leaves ×1 is the plan drifting from the work.
dash_trend_none: No session has a logged time yet. A course's line starts at {min} logged.
dash_trend_wait: The line starts once {min} are logged: {left} to go.
dash_trend_axis: Across: how many of the course's sessions were logged by then.
help_trend: Each course with logged time gets its own panel. Across is how many of its sessions are logged, up is its typical session at that point: the geometric mean of real ÷ planned, on a log scale every panel shares. The band is the 95% interval: wide at first, it narrows as the logged sessions agree. A line that stays away from ×1 is a lasting bias of the plan rather than chance, and a reason to change the length of the sessions ahead. The line starts at 6 logged: with fewer there is no interval. Hover a panel to read its values, or Tab to it and walk the line with the arrow keys, Home and End; the table under the panels lists them all.
dash_modules_hint: The plan estimated modules, not sessions: a session can end on time and leave its module's goal to an added one. Here are the hours a module was first planned with against those logged on all its sessions, added ones included. A ratio appears once every session of the module is done with a logged time and the last one met its goal.
dash_modules_none: No module has a done session yet.
unfinished_label: Goal not met: continues next time
unfinished_add: Add a session to finish it
focus_check_title: Were you working all of this?
focus_check_hint: The stopwatch counted {time} against a plan of {planned}.
focus_check_why: A stopwatch left running moves a course's pace more than anything, so check the time first.
focus_adjust_title: How long did it really take?
focus_adjust_hint: {time} is logged. Choose the time you really worked.
dash_forecast_hint: How long a planned hour really takes, judging by the time you logged, and when the rest will be finished at that pace.
dash_pace_if_planned: {pace} if the rest took their plan
pace_wait_n: a pace from {min} logged, {count} so far
dash_forecast_none: Log the time you spent in a session's card and the forecast will appear here.
dash_forecast_miss: the forecast is {count} d past it

catchup_nothing: Nothing is missed and your pace matches the plan: there is nothing to change.
catchup_keep: Leave the plan as it is
catchup_push_hint: Every open session slides to the next study days. The weekly load stays, the plan ends later.
catchup_squeeze: Make it up in the coming weeks

catchup_unplaced: No room was found for {count} sessions
catchup_pace: Give the sessions the time they really take
catchup_pace_hint: Every session ahead gets the length its course's pace asks for. The days stay; a day's sessions follow one another.
catchup_hint_pace: Nothing is missed, but your pace differs from the plan. The option is applied as one step and can be undone from the history.
zoom_in: Zoom in: more room per hour
zoom_out: Zoom out: more hours on screen

focus_hint: One session and a stopwatch: the time it really takes is logged in the plan.
focus_expand_hint: The stopwatch across the whole window: no header or navigation
focus_empty: Every session of the plan is done.
reviews_offer: The module “{title}” is done. Plan three short reviews so it stays in memory?
export_alarms: Add a reminder {minutes} minutes before each start

ai_request_placeholder: Add the course … on Tuesdays and Thursdays at 19:00, starting in March
ai_with_notes: With the notes of events (several times longer)

ai_invalid: No update found in the text: {reason}
ai_nothing: This update changes nothing in the plan.
ai_applied: Applied. Every change is a step of the history: Undo takes them back one by one.
ai_read_only: The plan is read-only here: the update can be checked but not applied.
zone_example: A session the plan has at {plan} starts at {there} in {city}.
zone_search: City, country or offset: Warsaw, Poland, UTC+1

help_toggle: Help marks: what is on this page
icons_only_hint: Buttons with an icon hide their word: it shows on hover
help_views:
Day, week, month, year and the whole plan as a list. Keys D, W, M, Y, L switch the view, the ← → arrows move by a period, and the date in the title opens a day picker.
On a wide screen there are also the time scale (+ and −), Work week, 24 hours and Expand, which gives the calendar the whole window.
help_event:
Three ways to add an event: the Event button, a double click on a free slot, or dragging across a day; the form opens beside it.
The fastest is a line in the search (Ctrl/⌘ K or /): “Review tomorrow 14:00 1h”. The same search finds events and commands.
help_calendars:
Every course is a calendar with its own color. A click on a chip hides or shows it, the eye on the chip (or a double click) leaves it alone, and Show all brings the rest back.
Labels, above the chips once some calendar has one, show only the calendars of one label; a second click shows them all again.
Calendars renames, recolors, reorders and adds them, gives them labels, and hides a calendar with all its events from every view: it stays in the plan and counts toward the week.
help_grid:
Drag an event to another time or day; drag an edge to change its length. One repeat of a repeating event moves alone, the others stay.
With the keyboard: Alt + arrows move, Alt Shift ↑ ↓ change the length, Delete sends it to the trash. The number next to a weekday is the hours of study that day.
help_more: In the ⋮ menu: the history of changes, the trash (keeps what was removed for 30 days), shifting the plan by some days, Catch up, a second time zone, your real calendar in grey behind the plan, reminders 10 minutes before a start, and the list of keys.
help_history: Every change is a step you can take back and redo: the arrows here, Ctrl/⌘ Z and Ctrl/⌘ Shift Z. The History window (key H) returns the plan to any point; the last 100 steps are kept.
help_next:
The session going on now, or the next one with a countdown. Start in focus opens a page with a stopwatch: Finish marks the session done and logs the time it really took.
Today lists every event of the day with its state. A session not done yet has its own focus button, and ⋮ marks it done (asking the time it took), skips it, or moves it to the next free slot. A skipped session is no longer open work but counts as missed.
help_budget:
The hours of study planned for this week against the plan's budget; the gym and the Saturday buffer do not count. Below are the goals the schedule implies: they tick themselves as sessions are done.
Week review sums the week up and offers ways to catch up.
help_courses: The ring is the share of a course's hours that are done. Under the name: sessions done, the day the course ends and your pace (real hours per planned hour) when it differs from the plan. Next opens the next open session.
help_map: Every week of the plan in one strip: the height of a bar is the hours of that week, red means over the budget. A click opens that week in the calendar.
help_dates: A month to navigate with: a click on a day opens it in the calendar, a click on a week number opens the whole week. Days with sessions are marked.
help_runway: On the left, the days left until the deadline and whose deadline it is; Set up chooses the course and its day. The strip shows the stages of that course in order, the circles are labs and checkpoints, and the red mark is today. A click on a circle opens its event.
help_file_title: Plan file, AI chat and export
help_file:
Plan file shows the plan as an overview, a list of events and JSON; its Library tab keeps plan files with versions and compares them, and its AI chat tab gives a text for any language model and applies the answer as steps you can undo.
Export to calendar sends the courses to Google, Outlook or Apple Calendar.
help_burnup: Two lines of hours added up: what the plan expects by each day and what is really done. Your line above the planned one means you are ahead, below it means behind. The dashed part continues your real pace to the end of the plan. The band by the dashed line runs from the day half of the simulated futures are done to the day nine in ten are.
help_forecast: When a session is marked done, its card takes the time it really took. From that comes the pace of a course, real hours per planned hour, and the day the rest of the course would end at that pace. The margin is the days left before the deadline. The pace counts only sessions whose time was logged, and only once a course has {count} of them: until then the forecast follows the plan. Under the forecast is a range. It comes from 1,000 simulated futures, in each of which a session takes its plan times a ratio drawn from the course's logged times (from every course's while it has fewer than {count}; none older than six months). Half of the futures end by the first date, nine in ten by the second. The less is logged, the wider the range.
help_weekly: A bar is the hours of one week and its colors are the courses. The line is the weekly budget: anything above it is overload. Hover a bar for the numbers; the same data is in the table under the chart.
help_focus: One session and a stopwatch. Start runs the time and pause holds it; the stopwatch survives a reload. Finish marks the session done and logs the minutes it took, with when it began and how long it stood paused, which feeds your pace on the Progress page. The hourglass beside the digits counts down the planned session, or work blocks of 25 + 5, 50 + 10 or your own rhythm: when the sand runs out it chimes, and a break pours through the glass too. The tab title shows the minutes left.

help_ai_title: How to work with an AI chat
help_ai:
1. Write what to change, or pick a ready request and replace what is in angle brackets.
2. Copy the brief puts the rules of the plan, the plan itself and your request on the clipboard; paste it into any chat.
3. Paste the chat's answer on the right. The page shows what would be added, removed and changed, and warns about overloaded weeks.
4. Apply stores the changes as history steps: each can be undone. If the answer does not fit, copy the request to fix it and send it to the same chat.

free_slot_none: There is no free time inside the budget in the next four weeks.
copy_link: Copy a link to the event

google_setup_hint: Connecting takes an OAuth client of your own in Google Cloud. It is made once, in about ten minutes:
google_step_api: Turn on the Google Calendar API. Google offers to make a project for it.
google_step_auth: In Google Auth Platform, press Get started: any app name, your own address. Pick the Personal audience if it is offered; otherwise External, then Publish app on the Audience page.
google_step_scope: Under Data access, add this scope and save:
google_step_client: Under Clients, create one of type Web application with this authorized redirect URI:
google_step_load: Load the JSON file Google offers when the client is made, or paste its ID and secret.
google_file_wrong: There is no OAuth client in this file. Use the JSON Google offers when the client is made.
google_file_redirect: This client does not list the redirect URI above, so Google will refuse the sign-in. Add it to the client first.
google_file_desktop: This is a Desktop app client. Google may refuse it here; a Web application client with the redirect URI above is the sure way.
sync_client_kept: Both stay on this computer, in a file git does not track.
google_problem_api: The Google Calendar API is off in the client's Cloud project.
sync_hint: The plan is kept in calendars of its own in your {app} account. What you change there comes into the plan by itself, and Undo takes it back.
sync_reconnect: {app} ended the sign-in. Connect again to keep the calendars in step: nothing is lost meanwhile.
sync_problem_client: {app} did not accept this client's ID or secret. Enter the client again, or use another one.
sync_problem_scope: Access to the calendars was left out on {app}'s page. Connect again and allow it.
sync_problem_offline: {app} cannot be reached right now. The planner tries again by itself.
sync_denied: Signing in was cancelled on {app}'s page.
sync_connect_failed: Signing in to {app} did not work. Check the client and try again.
sync_read_only: The plan cannot be changed here, so it is not kept in {app}.
sync_review_bar: Changes from your calendars that need a decision: {count}
sync_review_hint: These were not taken into the plan by themselves. Keep plan writes the plan's version back to the calendar; taking the calendar's version stores the change, and Undo takes it back.
sync_deleted: Deleted in {app}: the session would go to the trash
outlook_setup_hint: Connecting takes an app registration of your own in Microsoft Entra, free with a work, school or personal Microsoft account. It is made once, in about five minutes:
outlook_step_register: Under App registrations, press New registration and give it any name. For Supported account types, pick the one that includes personal Microsoft accounts.
outlook_step_redirect: In the same form, under Redirect URI, choose Web and paste this address, then press Register:
outlook_step_secret: Under Certificates & secrets, add a New client secret and copy its Value, not the Secret ID: it is shown only once.
outlook_step_paste: Paste the Application (client) ID from the app’s Overview page, and the secret.
outlook_work_note: With a work or school account, an administrator may have to approve the app first.
outlook_problem_mailbox: This Microsoft account has no Outlook mailbox to keep calendars in. Connect another account.
integrations_hint: Keep the plan in step with your calendar app, see your own busy time behind it, or take it away as files.
integrations_export: Files to import once: an .ics for each calendar, or one for all
timeline_page_hint: Every course on its lane. Drag a course, its end or its ◆ deadline, or pick a course and change it on the panel. Changes gather in a draft and are saved only when you press Apply.
timeline_expand_hint: The timeline across the whole window: no header or hint
timeline_pick: Pick a course on the timeline: its dates, deadline and spare days show here, with ways to change them.
timeline_problem: The draft does not fit the plan: {reason}
timeline_leave_text: The draft is not stored: leaving drops it.
labels_hint: Group courses by provider or program; a course can carry several labels. They filter the planner, group the timeline and give totals on Progress.
label_delete: Remove the label {label} from every calendar

dash_first_label: Each course counts under its first label.
skip_session_hint: Not doing it: it leaves the open work and counts as missed
move_next_free: Move to the next free slot
